business.text: Alphabet is Google: search and search advertising, YouTube, Android, Chrome, Google Cloud, and the Gemini AI models, plus Waymo and other bets.

guidance_diff.why: The last two 8-K Exhibit 99.1 press releases for this name have not been pulled from EDGAR, so there is no mechanical guidance diff. This is the free substitute for a transcript: it carries the guidance figures and none of the questions.
guidance_diff.caveat: Mechanical. Two press releases, sentences with a forward-looking word and a figure, matched on metric and period. It does not read tone, it cannot see a guide given without a number, and a filer that changes how it names a period between releases shows one lapsed and one introduced where a reader would see one reiterated. The verbatim sentence sits under every row so the machine's reading can be checked.

earnings_text.text: Q2 2026 (July 22, 2026): revenue $119.8 billion vs $117.0 billion consensus, up 24%; Cloud up 82%; EPS $9.11. Shares fell 3.7% after hours on capex concerns. Q1 2026 showed a similar beat with Cloud acceleration and a muted reaction.

read.prior_quarter_label: Q1 2026 — named only as "Q1 2026 showed a similar beat with Cloud acceleration and a muted reaction", with no figures
read.headline: Q2 2026 revenue of $119.8bn beat the $117.0bn consensus and grew 24% with Cloud up 82%, and the stock still fell 3.7% after hours on capex concerns.

guidance.what: AI capex — "roughly $180 billion" (not framed as guidance in the note)
guidance.detail: This figure appears once, parenthetically, inside a bear-case sentence. The note does not attribute it to management, does not name a period (annual, cumulative, actual or planned), does not give a prior-period figure to compare it against, and never calls it forward-looking. It cannot be scored as raised, cut or maintained.
guidance.quote: Every dollar of AI capex (roughly $180 billion) is a dollar the market once counted as free cash flow

guidance.what: Cloud backlog — $514 billion (a disclosed balance in the note, not framed as guidance)
guidance.detail: Given in the "Why it is on the list" section alongside "revenue grew 24% last quarter". The note gives no as-of date for the backlog, no prior-period backlog, and no conversion or duration commentary, so no direction of change can be established.

tone.assessment: Constructive on the business, non-committal on the entry price. The note is bullish on quality and growth (rank 32 of 150, "compounder" bucket, Cloud as "a second engine") but explicitly withholds a buy at the current price, resolving to a conditional "pullback buy" with mid-range conviction (3 of 5) and a buy zone of $300 to $335 that sits below the quoted price of 342.48.
tone.evidence: The upside is real but the entry is average, so it is a pullback buy.
tone.confidence: medium — this reads the tone of the note's author, not of management. The file contains no management quotes, no earnings-call commentary, no CEO or CFO remarks, and no prepared-remarks language anywhere; the words "guidance", "outlook", "management", "CEO" and "CFO" do not appear in it. Management's tone is therefore not assessable from this source at all, which caps confidence at what can be said about the write-up itself.

new_risks.risk: The balance sheet flipped from net cash to net debt between FY2024 and FY2025. Under the table's stated convention ("Net debt (USD bn, negative = net cash)"), FY2024's -73.08 is net cash of $73.08bn and FY2025's 15.84 is net debt of $15.84bn — a swing of roughly $89bn in one fiscal year. The note prints the table but never comments on this change.

Free cash flow was essentially flat in FY2025 (73.27) versus FY2024 (72.76) while revenue rose from 350.02 to 402.84. The bear case raises the capex-versus-free-cash-flow tradeoff in the abstract, but this specific stalling in the table is not cited there and is not named as a thesis killer.
The adtech remedies ruling could force an AdX divestiture.

dodged.topic: Nothing in this source can be attributed to management dodging anything
dodged.reasoning: The file is a third-party research write-up assembled from a stock screen and press coverage, not a transcript or a company release. It contains no management quotes, no call commentary, and no prepared remarks; "guidance", "outlook", "management", "CEO" and "CFO" do not appear in it. The entries below are therefore gaps in the NOTE, not established evasions by management — the note cannot settle that distinction.

dodged.topic: The adtech remedies proceeding is raised twice but never dated, sized, or sourced
dodged.reasoning: It appears in the bear case ("The adtech remedies ruling could force an AdX divestiture") and again as a thesis killer ("an adtech ruling that breaks up the ad stack"), yet the note gives no status, venue, timing, or probability, and no figure for what AdX contributes. The note's only antitrust source is titled "Google search antitrust case: appeal and remedies in 2026" — the search matter, not the adtech matter — so the note carries no adtech-specific source behind a live thesis killer.

dodged.topic: Two of the note's own three thesis killers cannot be evaluated from the note
dodged.reasoning: Scored against the note's own list: (1) "search revenue growth under 5% for two quarters" — only one quarter of Search growth is given (17%, quarter unnamed), so the two-quarter condition cannot be evaluated, though that single reading is far above the threshold; (2) "an adtech ruling that breaks up the ad stack" — no status given, not evaluable; (3) "Cloud operating margin reversing" — the note gives Cloud operating income of $8.8bn against $24.8bn of quarterly revenue and $2.8bn "a year earlier", but no prior-year Cloud revenue, so no margin trend can be computed and "reversing" cannot be tested. The separate price trigger IS evaluable: price 342.48 on 2026-09-04 against a $260 close trigger.

dodged.topic: Capex is named as the cause of the share-price fall but never quantified for the quarter
dodged.reasoning: The note says shares fell 3.7% after hours on capex concerns, yet gives no capex figure for Q2 2026 and no period for the "roughly $180 billion" cited in the bear case. The reader is told what the market reacted to without being given the number it reacted to.

dodged.topic: Every business named outside Search and Cloud is left with no economics
dodged.reasoning: YouTube, Gemini, Waymo and "other bets" are each mentioned exactly once, in the one-line "What the company does" description; Android and Chrome appear a second time only as things the December 2025 judgment left intact. No revenue, growth, margin, or profit figure is attached to any of them anywhere in the file.

dodged.topic: The segment figures are never tied to a named quarter
dodged.reasoning: Search "$63.3 billion" is labeled "last quarter" and Cloud "$24.8 billion" is labeled "quarterly revenue", with no quarter named for either. The $119.8bn total is labeled Q2 2026 in a different section. The note never states that these belong to the same quarter, so the segments cannot be reconciled against the total.

Cloud operating income ($8.8bn) and Cloud revenue ($24.8bn) appear in the same sentence, but the prior-year comparison is income only ($2.8bn a year earlier) with no prior-year Cloud revenue, so no margin trend can be computed.
The as-of date for the $514 billion Cloud backlog, its prior-period value, and its expected conversion period.
The period covered by the "roughly $180 billion" capex figure, and whether it is annual or cumulative, actual or planned, and whose figure it is.

Q1 2026 specifics. It is described only as "a similar beat with Cloud acceleration and a muted reaction" — no revenue, EPS, consensus, or growth figures.
Revenue, profit, growth, or any economics for YouTube, Android, Chrome, Gemini, Waymo, or "other bets", including whether any of them is loss-making.
Whether the 3.7% after-hours decline persisted or reversed. The note gives price 342.48 on 2026-09-04 with a -17% drawdown from the 52 week high but never connects that to the July 22 reaction.

Whether the December 2025 judgment's data sharing and default restrictions have taken effect, and any effect on results. The note also does not say what the Apple renegotiations concern.

Buybacks, dividends, headcount, tax rate, or currency effects — none are mentioned. Diluted shares do decline across the table (13,159 in FY2022 to 12,230 in FY2025), but the note never comments on the cause.

Analyst estimate breadth or revision counts. The note gives only "Next fiscal year EPS estimate moved +2.7% in 90 days"; the words "analysts" and "revisions", and any up/down revision counts, do not appear in the file.
Consensus for anything other than Q2 2026 revenue ($117.0bn). No EPS consensus is given, so the $9.11 EPS cannot be scored as a beat or miss.
Any fiscal data before FY2022 — the note states "Four fiscal years is all the source provides."
Whether anything has changed since 2026-09-04. All four sources are marked read or pulled 2026-09-04 and next earnings is 2026-10-28, so nothing in the file post-dates that pull.
read.market_reaction: The only reaction datum for the quarter is that shares fell 3.7% after hours on capex concerns, despite the revenue beat ($119.8bn vs $117.0bn consensus) and 24% growth. For the prior quarter the note says only that Q1 2026 "showed a similar beat with Cloud acceleration and a muted reaction". Separately, the screen line records price 342.48 USD on 2026-09-04, -17% from the 52 week high and -16% from the all time high, but the note never links that drawdown to the July 22 earnings reaction. That price sits above the note's own buy zone of $300 to $335 and well above its $260 price trigger.

read.standing_caveat: A research note is already a summary, so its silence is usually the author compressing rather than management evading. Every entry under 'not addressed' below should be read at the confidence it states, and none of them is evidence about what was said on the call, because no transcript was available. See NOTES.md.

thesis.why_on_the_list: Compounder bucket, rank 32. Forward P/E 23.1, right at its four year median. Not cheap versus its own history, but revenue grew 24% last quarter with Cloud up 82% and a $514 billion Cloud backlog. It is on the list for quality and growth, with the entry point being the question.
thesis.business_quality: Search is still a 90% share product and grew 17% last quarter to $63.3 billion despite AI Overviews and chat competitors. Cloud has become a second engine: $24.8 billion of quarterly revenue with operating income of $8.8 billion versus $2.8 billion a year earlier. The December 2025 antitrust judgment left Chrome and Android intact but imposed data sharing and default restrictions. Insider ownership is about 1.6%.
thesis.verdict: Buy on pullback, November tranche or earlier if the zone is hit. Buy zone $300 to $335. Conviction 3 of 5.
thesis.action: Buy on pullback, November tranche or earlier if the zone is hit

logged.thesis: Revenue up 24%, Cloud up 82%, at its own median multiple. Good business, average price.
logged.wrong_if: Search growth under 5% twice, adtech breakup, or a close under $260.

The adtech remedies ruling could force an AdX divestiture. Cloud growth at 82% cannot last and will decelerate into a lower multiple.

multiples.label: Forward P/E
multiples.basis_note: The two sides are not the same multiple. The left is a forward P/E, the Street's estimate of next year's earnings. The median on the right is trailing: the price at each fiscal year end divided by that year's reported diluted EPS. Where earnings are expected to grow, forward is mechanically lower than trailing, so this column reads cheap by construction.

multiples.label: EV/EBITDA
multiples.basis_note: Both sides are trailing, so this comparison is like for like.

own_history.caveat: The median is taken at 4 fiscal year ends, so it is a 4-point median. That is a thin basis for 'cheap against its own history' and it says nothing about whether the old multiple was deserved.
own_history.basis_warning: Read the P/E row with care. Across the 136 names that carry both comparisons, 85% print a negative 'vs median' on forward P/E with a median of -29%, against 50% and 0.0% on EV/EBITDA where both sides are trailing. That gap is the basis mismatch, not 136 companies being cheap. It is also correlated with growth: faster-growing names look cheaper here (rank correlation -0.28 against revenue CAGR, versus -0.15 for EV/EBITDA), because their forward earnings are further above their trailing ones. The score weights the like-for-like EV/EBITDA comparison more heavily for exactly this reason.

drawdown.caveat: The all-time high is the highest closing price; the 52-week high is an intraday high. They are not on the same basis, and the drawdown from the all-time high is therefore understated.

price_basis.note: The drawdowns and the multiple-versus-median above were computed inside the price screen from its own last close, which is not quite the price shown at the top of this page: the two come from different passes of the pipeline and differ by a fraction of a percent. Neither is wrong; they are just not the same number.

peer_set.label: Communication Services
peer_set.caveat: Not enough names in its industry to compare against, so this is against 5 others in Communication Services. A sector holds businesses that are not really comparable, so read the percentile loosely.

peers.verdict: priced above where its quality sits
peers.reasoning: It is the dearest quartile on price and mid-pack on quality, 50 points apart the other way: it is priced above where its measured characteristics rank among its peers. Sometimes that is the market seeing something these measures do not; sometimes it is not.
peers.why: The own-history comparison above says nothing about whether the old multiple was deserved. This asks a different question: where does this name sit among its peers on price, and where does it sit among them on the things a price is supposed to reflect.

written_view.text: At $342 and 23.1x forward the stock sits at its own median and above Microsoft and Meta. Three year view with 15% EPS growth: bear 18x on trough growth is roughly $330, flat; base 22x is about $520; bull 26x is about $620. The upside is real but the entry is average, so it is a pullback buy.

score.caveat: A percentile against 150 names on one date. It has not been backtested; see the positioning page for why not.
